text:
Ottawa led Philadelphia 5-3 on Thursday and lost 6-5 in overtime, the kind of night that stings even inside a seven-game point streak (5-0-2). The Senators had been winning all the races early, as PHLY's Charlie O'Connor put it when Dylan Cozens scored, and still let it slip.

The good news is that the streak is built on play. Ottawa got 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) during the run, and 53% for the season, with 54% at five on five. Goals for and against both sit close to what the chances earned, so the 14-6-3 record is honest. Our odds put them 89% to make the playoffs.

Travis Green has depth that works. Claude Giroux, Michael Amadio and Ridly Greig have allowed almost nothing together, 80% of the chances in a small sample. Cozens, Tim Stützle and Fabian Zetterlund are at 68%, and Thomas Chabot with Jordan Spence have been on for 17 goals for and 7 against. Philip Tomasino, on a line with Shane Pinto and Drake Batherson, is making the most of his chance, as Coming Down the Pipe's Graeme Nichols put it.

The month has had human stories too. Tyler Boucher scored the winner in his NHL debut with his father Brian watching, and Nick Cousins was ruled out 7 to 10 days after a big hit from Jakob Chychrun, per DAZN. What we'd watch is the third periods: a team this good at driving play shouldn't be giving back two-goal leads.
headline: The Senators keep earning their points
